attempts.summary: Configured a 3-node MariaDB 10.6 Galera cluster (node1, node2, node3) on RHEL 7.9. Since RHEL 7 is EOL for the official MariaDB repo tooling and had no base OS repo configured, I manually pointed yum at the MariaDB archive (archive.mariadb.org, mariadb-10.6/rhel7-amd64) plus a CentOS 7 vault base repo (node3 only, for missing perl/libaio/boost deps), installed MariaDB-server + galera-4, opened firewalld ports 3306/4567/4568/4444, and wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on each node with wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3 and rsync-based SST. Bootstrapped node1 with galera_new_cluster, then started node2 and node3 which joined via SST, reaching a 3-node Synced/Primary cluster. Verified multi-master write propagation (writes from each of the 3 nodes visible on the others). Demonstrated availability during a member outage: stopped node3, confirmed the cluster stayed Primary at cluster_size=2, wrote a row via node1, restarted node3, and confirmed it automatically resynced (IST) back to Synced/cluster_size=3 with the row present. Then executed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id + wsrep health on all 3 nodes, restarted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially via `systemctl reboot` (one at a time, quorum preserved throughout — never below 2/3), polled each until exec was available again, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed each node's mariadb.service was active and rejoined the cluster (Synced/Primary/size=3) before moving to the next. A final post-restart write/read check across all three nodes confirmed the cluster still works end-to-end. Root and SST credentials were generated on-node and only ever passed via secret_env in later commands (not left in final report).
